Resolves #18626

A grid can select nothing: `body: {selectionModel: false}` leaves the View and every body without a model — nothing is instantiated, no row is ever marked, no selection handler is installed. The default (an omitted `selectionModel` → one `RowModel`, created by the center body and hoisted to the View) and an explicit model config are unchanged. The locked bodies stop instantiating the transient `RowModel` each of them created on the way to receiving the View's single instance: they are created with `false`, and `applyViewSelectionModel()` hands them the instance. The hoist honors `null` as the third state on both timings, so a post-construction `false` clears the View and every body and destroys the one model.

Evidence: L2 (unit arms on real `grid.Container` instances with locked start and end bodies; the owning tree `unit/grid` + `unit/selection` 103/103) → L2 required (every AC is a construction-time or unit-observable engine contract). Residual: none, Residual-Owner: none.

Intake: self-authored 2026-09-12 in an earlier session — the drift probe (`git log origin/dev --since=<createdAt> --name-only` ∩ `src/grid/Body.mjs`, `src/grid/View.mjs`, `src/grid/Container.mjs`, `src/util/ClassSystem.mjs`) came back empty at `dev@5dc6b80fef`, so no intake payload ran.

| AC-5 | red-first at `dev@5dc6b80fef`: the four new arms red (`4 failed / 2 passed` — the opt-out arm found a `RowModel` on every surface; default and explicit counted two transient `RowModel`s from the locked bodies; the dynamic arm found the old model alive) → `6 passed` after the change |

## Deltas from ticket
- The locked bodies are created with `false` (the ticket allowed keeping their internal `null`): a body defaults `null`, so each locked body instantiated a transient `RowModel` the hoist then replaced — the default and explicit arms count them (two on dev). `false` plus the hoist closes the "never let a body instantiate a second model" trap instead of stepping around it.
- `applyViewSelectionModel(null)` clears instead of returning early, so the opt-out is also a post-construction state ("one opt-out value the whole hoist honors"); a dynamic `null` keeps its old meaning — a fresh default. Bodies receive `false`, never `null`, from the hoist.
- `grid.View#beforeSetSelectionModel` normalizes every falsy value to `null` (it handed `false` through), and its JSDoc no longer says the View "defaults to a RowModel" — it never did; the center body does.
- `Body#onStoreRecordChange` reads `selectionModel?.ntype` — the one unguarded dereference a model-less body reached. The row paint already derives from `selectedRows` / `selectedCells`, which are `[]` without a model.

## Comments

### `@neo-fable-clio` commented on 2026-09-13T11:36:36Z

Superseded, not merged: the maintainer's design ruling (2026-09-13) — the View is in charge of selection, grid bodies carry no selection model at all — makes a body-level opt-out the wrong owner. #18626 is re-scoped to the View-owned shape (`viewConfig: {selectionModel: null}`, the body's config removed, the peer fan-out deleted); the successor PR follows on `agent/18626-view-owned-selection`. This branch stays as the measured dead end (the red-first arms counted the locked bodies' transient RowModels).
